title: The Educated Barbarian: Hagakure analysis (part. 20)
summary: NH reads Book Three of the Hagakure and draws lessons on always struggling, mastering pain, aiming beyond goals, confronting death, keeping vigour in old age, staying calm under adrenaline and approaching heavy weights with certainty. He ends with a contentious quote on reason and women and his evolutionary interpretation of it.
claims: In life the right option is always to fight; submitting to an aggressor only makes you weaker and more controlled
Never follow an attacker to a second location; resist on the spot
Pain is a mental stimulus; mastery means feeling it without letting it create mental anguish
Like cutting through to the ground or punching through a target, aim beyond your goal and you will reach it without noticing
Don't set deadlines for physique goals: they create stress and just lead to another deadline
Your ultimate physique or strength goal should be so far away you never reach it
For natural bodybuilding, being realistic just means low standards; realistic people stop pushing once they hit their limit
It's easy to claim you don't fear death or torture while healthy; the real test comes when it happens
Modern people are regressing by dying of illnesses created by overconsumption of food, drugs and alcohol
He would rather walk into the forest than linger once he can't take care of himself and loses his fire
Old men who keep their fire share three things: a lifelong uncompromised passion, staying physically active, and building families
If the body dies, the spirit dies with it, and vice versa
A virtuous patriarch or matriarch is one of the most beautiful things on earth
Blacking out or tunnel vision in a fight is poor self-mastery from uncontrolled adrenaline; you miss attacks from the side
Breathing and staying calm opens your vision and removes the stiffness that makes fighters slow
Football aggression gave him tunnel vision and made him a bad player, while in calmer basketball he could see the field
During warm-ups the bar feels similar from 400 to 440 lb because proprioception adapts, not because the weight changes
He used to obsess over whether he could lift a weight and sometimes failed lifts he should have made
Approach the bar knowing the programmed weight will go up; since adopting this he has never failed a deadlift or squat in his notebook
Contemplating death daily removes its power over you, since every human fear is ultimately fear of death
Losing your fear of death doesn't remove self-preservation; reason still keeps best practices to survive
Discrimination itself is neutral: separating things to protect self, family or society
Men evolved to discriminate threats more because they were more exposed to violence; women tend to be more open to new things
Women are the biggest target of advertising because they tend to be easier to influence
exercises: approach the bar certain it will go up
